features.name: Reporting
features.description:
Reporting Capabilities

Vendors should be evaluated on the richness and flexibility of their reporting features. This includes the ability to provide different levels of detail tailored to different user roles (e.g., administrators vs. executives). Solutions should offer out-of-the-box reporting templates such as capacity reports (covering total system capacity, used capacity, and unused capacity) and task reports (capturing execution status, task type, protected resources, execution time, processed data volume, and performance metrics). Beyond predefined templates, solutions should also support simplified tools for building custom reports to meet specific organizational needs.

Report Export & Integration

The ability to export reports in multiple formats such as PDF, Excel, or other commonly used formats is essential for sharing and compliance purposes. In addition, solutions should be assessed for whether they integrate with third-party reporting and analytics platforms, enabling advanced visualization, BI integration, and cross-system analysis.

Alerting & Notifications

Effective monitoring requires robust alerting mechanisms. Vendors should be evaluated on whether their solution supports multiple alert channels, including email, SMS/text messages, push notifications to mobile apps, alerts within the management console, and integration with ITSM systems for automatic ticket creation. This ensures that administrators receive timely notifications and can respond quickly to issues.

Capacity Planning

Another critical aspect is how the backup solution supports capacity planning. The evaluation should consider whether the solution provides predictive analytics, trending reports, or modeling capabilities to help administrators anticipate growth, optimize resource allocation, and avoid capacity bottlenecks.

features.name: Backup data migration to cloud
features.description:
Backup Data Migration Technologies

Vendors should be evaluated on their support for industry-standard data transfer technologies that enable movement of backup data to and from the cloud. This includes integration with AWS Snowball, Azure Data Box, and Google Cloud Storage Transfer Service to handle large-scale data transfers efficiently and securely.

Baseline Copy Transfers

Assess how the solution facilitates faster baseline copy transfers from the customer’s data center to the cloud. This may include seeding mechanisms, bandwidth optimization, deduplication, or compression to reduce transfer times and costs.

On-Premises to Cloud Copying Processes

Evaluate the flexibility of the solution in supporting multiple transfer modes when copying on-premises backups to public cloud storage. Specifically, whether transfers can be performed manually or automated via policies, enabling organizations to align cloud migration with operational policies and compliance requirements.

features.name: Scalability
features.description:
Cloud Scaling Capabilities

Vendors should be assessed on how their solution scales up and scales out in cloud environments. This includes whether scaling is automated or manual, and whether it is achieved by adding servers/nodes, launching additional instances, or other mechanisms. The evaluation should also consider how scaling meets performance expectations in public cloud environments and whether it is customer-initiated or dynamically managed by the platform. Ideally, vendors should provide detail on scaling behavior across each supported public cloud (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP).

Hybrid Cloud Deployments

Vendors should demonstrate proven scalability in large hybrid cloud deployments (covering on-premises, public cloud, and SaaS workloads). Evaluation should include details of their largest customer deployments, with specifics on protected workload counts, data sizes, backup compute and storage requirements, and how the solution achieves RTO/RPO compliance at scale.

On-Premises Scaling

Assessment should also cover how the solution scales when deployed on-premises, whether as an integrated appliance or a software-only deployment. This includes the ability to add compute and storage resources flexibly to handle growth, while maintaining performance and availability.

Block-level incremental backups for image-based backup
Incremental forever with full hydration (truly forever)
Incremental forever with regular full and full hydration
Incremental forever with synthetic full

features.name: Ransomware Detection capabilities
features.description:
Vendors should be evaluated on their ability to detect early indicators of ransomware or cyberattacks within the backup environment. This includes monitoring for:

Anomalous backup job size changes that may indicate active encryption of data.

Detection of encryption within backup data as a sign of a potential attack.

Entropy analysis within backup data to identify suspicious randomness patterns caused by encryption.

Real-time or near real-time monitoring of anomalous increases in write traffic on protected hosts as an early warning indicator.

Additional anomaly detection techniques provided by the vendor, beyond the above, to strengthen cyber resilience.

features.name: SIEM Integration
features.description:
SIEM Integration for Anomaly Alerts

Evaluate whether the BDPP solution integrates with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms to automatically generate alerts when anomalies or ransomware indicators are detected. Vendors should provide a list of supported SIEM platforms (e.g., Splunk, IBM QRadar, Microsoft Sentinel, ArcSight, etc.) to demonstrate interoperability with enterprise security monitoring workflows.

features.name: Malware scanning capabilities
features.description:
Anomaly & Ransomware Detection

Detect suspicious changes in backup job sizes, encryption within backup data, and entropy analysis as early signs of ransomware.

Monitor anomalous increases in write traffic in real time (or near real time) on protected hosts.

Scan incoming backup streams for ransomware using malware signatures.

Provide innovative anomaly detection processes designed to reduce false positives and improve detection accuracy.

Offer aids to quickly identify the last known good backup prior to data encryption or compromise.

Malware Scanning (Native & Third-Party)

Support vendor-developed scanning during backup operations, post-backup, and during recovery, with continuous updates to malware signatures.

Run signature-based scans of existing backup data, with the ability to automatically trigger re-scans whenever malware signatures are updated.

Enable integration with third-party malware scanners (e.g., Microsoft Defender, Symantec, CrowdStrike, McAfee) for layered protection.

Clearly detail capabilities of native malware scanners and supported third-party integrations.

Recovery Assurance & Threat Hunting

Provide mechanisms for identifying the last clean backup copy to ensure reliable restores.

Deliver advanced threat hunting capabilities within the backup environment, enabling investigation of attack patterns and compromise indicators.

Integrate with SIEM platforms (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, QRadar, ArcSight, etc.) for centralized alerting, monitoring, and incident correlation.

features.name: Support for Search, Data classification and Indexing
features.description:
Metadata Integration

Cross-SaaS Metadata Search: Assess whether the solution can integrate and correlate metadata across SaaS applications (e.g., finding all customer-related emails in Microsoft 365 alongside Salesforce records).

Cross-Source Metadata Search: Evaluate the ability to unify metadata across heterogeneous environments (e.g., discovering all versions of a file whether stored on-premises NAS or in OneDrive).

Search & Restore Capabilities

Search Scope: Determine whether searches can be performed across different data types and environments, including file backups (NAS), virtual machines, and within database content.

Search in Hybrid/Multi-Cloud Environments: Review how the solution handles differences or limitations when searching data stored across hybrid, multicloud, or SaaS platforms.

Search Results Handling: Evaluate options for restoring or exporting search results — for example, restoring directly into a folder or packaging them into a single downloadable file (such as a ZIP archive).
